subject.title: Large session count freezes the gateway: whole-store parse + structuredClone on every operation (SQLite backend, no cache)

question: Should the initial repair be limited to removing whole-store work from steady-state SQLite operations, with persistent snapshot deduplication deferred unless maintainers explicitly approve a storage-model change?
rationale: The immediate row-level path appears to be a bounded performance repair, while cache design and hash/reference-backed snapshot storage affect persistent data ownership and may require migration decisions.

options.title: Land row-level hot-path repair first
options.body: Profile and replace steady-state whole-store reads and updates with row-level access while preserving the existing persisted entry shape.

options.title: Sponsor a storage-model redesign
options.body: Also deduplicate large per-session snapshots through an explicitly designed and migration-safe persistent representation.

recommendation.title: Land row-level hot-path repair first
recommendation.body: Profile and replace steady-state whole-store reads and updates with row-level access while preserving the existing persisted entry shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent visible session-store history makes this the best available routing candidate, although direct feature-history verification is still needed.
